title: Protocol for RNA-seq library preparation starting from a rare muscle stem cell population or a limited number of mouse embryonic stem cells
protocol: Euthanize mice in accordance with approved protocols.
Isolate skeletal muscle tissue from euthanized mice.
Digest isolated muscle tissue following the described protocol.
Perform antibody staining on digested muscle cells.
Conduct flow activated cell sorting (FACS) to isolate MuSCs.
Culture and maintain isolated MuSCs for further analysis.
Dissect muscle tissue with small scissors and collect it in cold DMEM with 1% P/S into 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Decant the muscle into a petri dish and remove the DMEM 1% P/S completely.
Mince the muscle using small scissors and razor blades until small pieces are achieved.
Place minced muscle into new 50 mL Falcon tubes with the digestion mix, composed of Ham’s F10 medium containing 5 mg/mL liberase, 0.4 mM CaCl2, 5 mM MgCl2, and 0.3% dispase.
Incubate samples in a shaking water bath at 37°C for 1–2 hours.
Centrifuge the cells at 50 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the supernatant and discard the pellet.
Optional: wash the pellet and collect the supernatant again to improve cell recovery.
Filter the supernatant through a 100 μm strainer filter into new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Filter the supernatant from step one through a 70 μm strainer filter into new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Centrifuge the filtered sample at 670 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Gently resuspend the cells in 2 mL of lysis buffer to lyse red blood cells, following manufacturer’s recommendations.
Incubate the resuspended cells on ice for 10 minutes.
Add 40 mL of cold FACS buffer composed by PBS supplemented with 2.5% fetal bovine serum (FBS) to the lysed sample.
Filter the sample through a 40 μm strainer filter into new 50 mL Falcon tubes.
Count the cells in the filtered sample.
Centrifuge the counted cells at 670 g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the cells to achieve a concentration of 1×10^6 cells/mL in FACS buffer.
Consecutively filter the supernatant through a 100 μm strainer.
Filter the filtered supernatant through a 70 μm strainer.
Centrifuge the sample at 670 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Resuspend the cells in 2 mL of lysis buffer to lyse red blood cells, following manufacturer’s recommendations.
Incubate the resuspended cells for 10 minutes on ice.
Add 40 mL of cold FACS buffer to the lysed cell suspension.
Filter the mixture through a 40 μm strainer into a new 50 mL Falcon tube.
Count the filtered cells.
Centrifuge the counted cells at 670 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuged cells.
Resuspend the cells in FACS buffer to achieve a concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Stain the sample with PE-Cy7-conjugated anti-CD45 antibody for 30 minutes on ice, protected from light.
Stain the sample with PE-Cy7-conjugated anti-Sca-1 antibody for 30 minutes on ice, protected from light.
Stain the sample with PE-Cy7-conjugated anti-CD31 antibody for 30 minutes on ice, protected from light.
Stain the sample with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-CD34 antibody for 30 minutes on ice, protected from light.
Stain the sample with PE-conjugated anti-ITGA7 antibody for 30 minutes on ice, protected from light.
Wash the stained cells with 40 mL of cold PBS.
Centrifuge the washed cells at 670 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the sample in 0.5 mL of cold PBS if cell yield is less than or equal to 1 million; add more PBS if necessary for higher yields.
Filter the resuspended cells through a test tube with a cell strainer cap to eliminate aggregates.
Stain the filtered cells with DAPI at a final concentration of 1 μg/mL for 5 minutes before FACS analysis.
Collect 200 cells of distinct MuSCs populations from the same sample based on CD34 and ITGA7 expression markers.
Employ FACS Aria II sorter for cell sorting with 4-way purity precision mode.
Use side scatter (SSC-A), forward scatter (FSC-A), and DAPI staining to exclude aggregates, debris, and dead cells.
Select PE-Cy7+ events for lineage-negative selection.
Identify CD34+ and ITGA7+ populations through double positive staining with Alexa Fluor 647+ and PE+ markers.
Sort MuSCs directly into PCR tubes pre-filled with 10 μl of Reaction buffer.
Employ the Takara “SMART-Seq v4 Ultra Low Input RNA Kit for Sequencing” to generate full-length cDNAs from FACS-isolated MuSCs.
Prepare a stock solution of 10× Reaction Buffer by mixing 19 μL of the 10× Lysis Buffer with 1 μL of the RNase inhibitor.
Dilute the 10× Reaction Buffer with nuclease-free water to make a 1× Reaction Buffer.
Place 10 μL of the 1× Reaction Buffer directly into an individual 0.2 mL RNase-free PCR tube.
Resuspend stained cells in PBS and sort 200 MuSCs into an RNase-free PCR tube with 9 μL of 1× Reaction Buffer.
Incubate the cell:reaction buffer mix at approximately 25°C for 5 minutes.
Place the samples on ice and add 2 μl of 3′ SMART-Seq CDS Primer II A.
Mix by gentle vortexing.
Spin the tube(s) briefly to collect the contents at the bottom of the tube.
Bring the final volume to 12.5 μl by adding additional Nuclease-Free Water if necessary.
Incubate the tubes at 72°C in a preheated, hot-lid thermal cycler for 3 minutes.
Place the samples on ice for 2 minutes immediately after incubation.
Preheat the thermal cycler to 42°C.
Add 2 μL per reaction, plus 10%, of the SMARTScribe Reverse Transcriptase to the Master Mix just before use.
Gently mix the reverse transcriptase tube without vortexing before adding it.
Mix the Master Mix well by gently vortexing.
Spin the tube(s) briefly in a minicentrifuge to collect the contents at the bottom of the tube.
Add 7.5 μl of the Master Mix to each reaction tube.
Gently pipette the contents of the tubes.
Spin the tubes briefly to collect the contents at the bottom of the tubes.
Place the tubes in a thermal cycler with a heated lid preheated to 42°C.
Run the PCR program as specified in the protocol table.
Thaw all reagents needed for PCR on ice, excluding the enzyme.
Gently vortex each reagent tube to mix and spin down briefly.
Store the prepared reagents on ice.
Prepare PCR Master Mix by combining specified reagents in the order shown.
Add 30 μl of PCR Master Mix to each tube containing 20 μL of first-strand cDNA product.
Place the samples in a preheated thermal cycler with a heated lid and run the program as instructed.
Purify the amplified cDNA using the Agencourt AMPure XP Kit according to manufacturer instructions.
Mix 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube with 250 μl Trizol for RNA extraction.
Thaw Trizol samples at approximately 25°C if frozen.
Let thawed samples stand at approximately 25°C for 5-10 minutes before proceeding.
Pre-spin the 5PRIME Phase Lock Heavy Gel tubes at 1,600 g for 45 seconds to collect gel on tube bottoms.
Add cells lysed in Trizol to the pre-spun 5PRIME Phase Lock Heavy Gel tubes.
Incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at approximately 25°C.
Manually invert the tubes 5 times after adding 100 μl Chloroform.
Incubate the inverted tubes at approximately 25°C for 10 minutes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 12,000 g at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Recover and transfer the transparent aqueous phase with a 20 μl pipette.
Add 10 μg of molecular grade glycogen (or GlycoBlue) to samples.
Add 250 μl of molecular grade isopropanol to the sample.
Invert tube 10 times to mix.
Let samples precipitate at -20°C for 12–18 h.
Centrifuge at 12,000 g, 4°C, for 30–45 min.
Gently discard the supernatant leaving approximately 10–15 μl behind.
Add 500 μl of freshly prepared 75% EtOH.
Mix 10 times by inversion.
Centrifuge at 7,500 g, 4°C for 5 minutes.
Gently discard the supernatant leaving approximately 10–15 μl behind without disturbing the pellet.
Remove most of the residual EtOH with a p10 pipette leaving 2–5 μl of EtOH.
Air dry the RNA pellet for about 15–20 minutes.
Resuspend the RNA pellet in 15 μL of RNase/DNase free water.
Keep the resuspended RNA on ice and immediately proceed to the next step.
Remove as much ethanol as possible using a 10 μL pipette before air-drying the pellet for approximately 5 minutes.
Air dry the pellet in a clean, RNase-free location.
Proceed with DNase treatment using a commercially available kit.
Quantify total RNA using a Qubit instrument.
Analyze the quality of the RNA using a Fragment Analyzer.
Enrich 10–250 μg of RNA for mRNAs by polyadenylation selection.
Convert enriched mRNA to cDNA.
Fragment the resulting cDNA.
Prepare First-Strand Reaction Buffer according to manufacturer instructions in a nuclease-free microcentrifuge tube.
Prepare Random Primer Mix according to manufacturer instructions in a nuclease-free microcentrifuge tube.
Keep the mix on ice until mRNA is purified.
Dilute total RNA with nuclease-free water to a final volume of 50 μl in a nuclease-free PCR tube.
Prepare and wash oligo-dT beads according to manufacturer instructions.
Add 50 μl beads to each RNA sample.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down six times.
Incubate at ∼25°C for 5 min.
Move the samples onto a magnetic rack to separate the beads.
Discard the supernatant.
Wash the beads twice according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Add 50 μl of Tris buffer to each tube.
Gently pipette up and down six times.
Place the tube on the thermocycler with the heated lid set at ≥ 90°C.
Run the specified program until the temperature reaches 25°C.
Remove the tube from the thermocycler when the temperature reaches 25°C.
Add 50 μl of RNA Binding Buffer (2×) to the samples.
Mix by gently pipetting up and down six times.
Incubate the tube at ∼25°C for 5 min.
Place the tube on the magnetic rack at ∼25°C until the solution is clear.
Remove and discard the supernatant from the tube.
Do not disturb the beads during this step.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack.
Wash the beads by adding 200 μl of Wash Buffer.
Gently pipette the entire volume up and down six times.
Spin down the tube briefly to collect the liquid from the wall and lid of the tube.
Place the tube on the magnet at ∼25°C until the solution is clear (∼2 min).
Remove and discard all of the supernatants.
Remove the tube from the magnetic rack.
Add 11.5 μl of First-Strand Synthesis Reaction Buffer and Random Primer Mix to resuspend beads.
Incubate the sample in a thermal cycler with heated lid set at 105°C according to program.
Transfer the tube on ice for 1 min when cooled enough (∼65°C).
Collect fragmented mRNA by transferring 10 μl of supernatant to nuclease-free PCR tube.
Bring volume up to 10 μl if less than 10 μl with First-Strand Synthesis Reaction Buffer and Random Primer Mix.
Place the tube on ice for immediate proceeding to First Strand cDNA Synthesis.
Add 8 μL of Nuclease-free Water and 2 μL of NEBNext First-Strand Synthesis Enzyme Mix to samples.
Mix reaction by pipetting up and down 15 times.
Put the samples in a preheated thermocycler with heated lid set at ≥ 80°C according to program.
Perform Second Strand cDNA Synthesis immediately after first strand synthesis.
Assemble second strand cDNA synthesis reaction on ice.
Add 8 μL of NEBNext Second Strand Synthesis Reaction Buffer and 48 μL of Nuclease-free Water to samples.
Mix the reaction by pipetting up and down 15 times.
Put the samples in a thermocycler set for 1 hour at 16°C with the heated lid at ≤ 40°C.
Purify the obtained cDNAs using SPRIselect Beads according to NEB instructions.
Quantify the synthesized cDNAs by Qubit or Picogreen.
Convert the quantified cDNAs into a library using the “NEBNext Ultra II DNA library prep for Illumina” kit following manufacturer’s instructions.
Dilute adapters 25 times and use 9 cycles of PCR for libraries amplification.
Enrich mRNAs by polyadenylation selection (step 42, RNA Extraction by Trizol).
Convert enriched mRNAs to cDNA.
Fragment the cDNAs using NEB buffers and enzymes included in the “NEBNext Ultra II RNA Library Prep Kit for Illumina”.
Quantify the final libraries by Picogreen.
Determine the size distribution of the final libraries on a Fragment Analyzer.
Libraries are equalized to the same molarity.
Pool libraries for sequencing on a NextSeq500 or NovaSeq3000.
Sequence samples at a depth of approximately 40 M reads per sample.
